title: Anthropic Office Suite: All 8 Claude Apps at $20 a Seat a Month
desc: Anthropic's office suite is 8 Claude apps: Docs, Slides and Design free, Sheets and Whiteboards from $17 a month, all 8 at $20 a seat a month billed yearly.
keywords: anthropic office suite, anthropic office tools, claude office suite, claude sheets, claude whiteboards, claude meetings, claude docs, claude slides, claude artifacts, claude for microsoft 365, claude for google workspace, claude team plan price, claude vs microsoft 365 copilot, claude vs google workspace gemini
question: What is in Anthropic's Claude office suite, and what does it cost per user?
cta: Planning to roll out Claude's office apps?
body:
Short answer. Anthropic's "office suite" is not one product: it is eight apps inside Claude (Docs, Slides, Design, Data, Sheets, Whiteboards, Motion and Meetings) plus Claude add-ins for Microsoft 365 and Google Workspace, rounded out by launches on November 10 and 12, 2026. Docs, Slides and Design are free; Sheets, Whiteboards, Data and the add-ins start with Pro at $17 a month billed yearly; and every app, Meetings included, comes with a Team standard seat at $20 a user a month billed yearly ($25 monthly). Anthropic lists no email, file storage or video calling of its own, so the suite sits on top of Microsoft 365 or Google Workspace, which cost $23.50 a user a month (Business Standard with Copilot) and $14 a user a month (Business Standard with Gemini) on yearly plans.

On 16 November 2026 we read Anthropic's launch posts, its Artifacts and pricing pages, the Claude Help Center and privacy center, and the business pricing pages of Microsoft and Google. Prices below are US list prices before tax. Several of these apps are in beta and change week to week, so check the linked pages before you buy.

What Anthropic actually calls it

Anthropic does not use the words office suite. Its own name for the apps inside Claude is Artifacts: the Claude Artifacts page lists seven types, and the November 10 announcement calls Sheets, Whiteboards and Data "new artifact types". The Verge headlined the same launch as Anthropic's own AI-powered office suite, and that is the phrase people now search.

Three more pieces carry their own names. Claude Meetings went into beta on November 12, 2026. Claude for Microsoft 365 and Claude for Google Workspace are add-ins that put Claude inside the Word, Excel or Google files you already keep.

Every app in the suite, in one list

  • Claude Docs. Briefs, reports and plans that you and Claude edit together, with comments. It exports to Word, PDF, Markdown or Google Docs (Help Center). It arrived on September 16, 2026 and left beta on October 8.
  • Claude Slides. Decks you can download as PowerPoint or PDF or export to Google Slides (October 8 post).
  • Claude Design. Mockups, one-pagers and visuals in your brand (Artifacts page).
  • Claude Data. The renamed Claude Dashboards, generally available since November 10. It needs a data connector such as a warehouse or CRM and builds dashboards and data stories (launch post).
  • Claude Sheets (beta). A spreadsheet Claude builds and edits with you, with 144 functions and up to 100,000 cells per sheet (Help Center). Our Claude Sheets guide covers what it cannot do yet.
  • Claude Whiteboards (beta). A shared board you can export as PNG. Boards can be sent to Lucid, Miro or Zoho Vani (Help Center).
  • Claude Motion (beta). Animated explainers you download as MP4, made without a video generation model (October 8 post). Team and Enterprise only.
  • Claude Meetings (beta). Claude joins a Google Meet call as a visible participant, takes notes and starts docs or whiteboards while you talk (product post). Our Claude Meetings guide has the setup steps.

Outside Claude, the Microsoft add-in has worked in Excel, PowerPoint and Word on paid plans since May 7, 2026, with Outlook in beta. The Google add-on reached Docs, Sheets and Slides in a public beta on October 6, 2026, on all paid plans. Both work in the file you already have open.

Which Claude plan includes which app

Claude planPrice per user a monthOffice apps included
Free$0Docs, Slides, Design
Pro$17 billed yearly ($200 up front), $20 monthlyFree apps plus Data, Sheets (beta), Whiteboards (beta), Claude for Microsoft 365 and Outlook, Claude for Google Workspace (beta)
Max$100, monthlySame apps as Pro, 5x Pro usage
Ultra$200, monthlySame apps as Pro, 10x Pro weekly usage
Team standard$20 billed yearly, $25 monthlyPro apps plus Motion (beta) and Meetings (beta); 2 to 150 people
Team premium$100 billed yearly, $125 monthlySame apps as standard, 5x standard usage
Enterprise$20 a seat billed yearly plus usage at API ratesTeam apps plus audit logs, SCIM, custom data retention and a HIPAA-ready option; 20 seat minimum

Prices and plan contents are from Anthropic's pricing page; the Google add-on's plans are from its launch post, and Meetings' plans from its Help Center guide. No app has its own price; each draws on your plan's usage limits, which Anthropic does not express as a message count. Meetings is the exception during the beta: notes, transcripts and answers that do not use connected tools are included on Team and Enterprise, and docs and whiteboards made in a call are free through February 10, 2027. Anthropic has not said what they will cost after that.

How it compares with Copilot and Gemini on price

OptionPer user a month, yearly billingWhat it covers
Google Workspace Business Starter$7 ($8.40 flexible)Gemini in Gmail and Vids, not in Docs, Sheets or Slides
Google Workspace Business Standard$14 ($16.80 flexible)Gemini in Gmail, Docs, Sheets, Slides, Drive, Meet and Chat
Claude Pro$17 ($20 monthly)Every Claude app except Meetings and Motion, plus both add-ins; no email or file storage service
Claude Team standard$20 ($25 monthly)All 8 Claude apps and both add-ins; no email or file storage service
Microsoft 365 Copilot Business add-on$21 ($18 first-year promotion)Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook and Teams, on top of an existing Microsoft 365 business plan
Google Workspace Business Plus$22 ($26.40 flexible)Same Gemini apps as Business Standard
Microsoft 365 Business Standard with Copilot$23.50Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, business email, Teams and Copilot
Microsoft 365 Business Premium with Copilot$32Microsoft 365 Business Premium with Copilot

The Microsoft prices are from its Copilot business pricing page. The $18 add-on price is a promotion that runs July 1 to December 31, 2026, applies to the first year only and is limited to existing Microsoft 365 business customers. Microsoft also bills some advanced AI features, such as Copilot Cowork and Autopilot, by usage on top of the license. Google's prices are from its Workspace pricing page, where the yearly commitment saves about 16% and new customers get 10% off Starter and Standard for 12 months on their first 20 users. Business Starter, Standard and Plus top out at 300 users on Google's page.

On scope, these are different kinds of product. Microsoft and Google sell the whole office: email, calendar, storage, video calls and the editors, with their assistant built in. Claude's suite is the assistant plus its own lighter editors, and Meetings joins Google Meet calls rather than hosting them. Where Claude is broader is that one seat works in both camps, in Excel and Word through one add-in and in Google Docs and Sheets through the other. Anthropic's May 7 post also says Microsoft 365 Copilot customers can use Claude models inside Excel and PowerPoint.

What a 10-person team would pay

Our arithmetic on the yearly list prices above, before tax and any usage charges:

  • Google Workspace Business Standard only: $1,680 a year.
  • Microsoft 365 Business Standard with Copilot only: $2,820 a year.
  • Claude Team standard only: $2,400 a year, or $3,000 on monthly billing, with no email or file storage service.
  • Google Workspace Business Standard plus Claude Team standard: $4,080 a year, or $34 a user a month.
  • An existing Microsoft 365 business plan plus the Copilot Business add-on: $2,520 a year on top of what you pay now, or $2,160 in the first year at the promotional price.

Adding Claude Team to Google Workspace takes the yearly bill from $1,680 to $4,080 and adds Sheets, Whiteboards, Meetings and Claude's models next to Gemini. In a Microsoft office, a Claude Team standard seat at $20 and the Copilot Business add-on at $21 list cost about the same per user, so the choice is about which assistant your team prefers.

Data and privacy terms to read before you sign up

  • Model training. On Team and Enterprise, Anthropic does not train on your content by default. If someone sends thumbs-up or thumbs-down feedback, that conversation can be kept for up to 5 years and used, and owners can switch the feedback button off (commercial privacy article). On Free, Pro and Max, chats are used to improve models if you allow it in your privacy settings, and incognito chats are not (consumer privacy article).
  • Sharing. On Team and Enterprise, artifact links stay inside your organization unless an owner turns on external sharing. On Free, Pro, Max and Ultra, anyone with the link can open what you share (Artifacts FAQ).
  • Meetings. Claude saves a transcript, summary and screen descriptions, not audio. Anthropic's product post says Claude stays out of calls with outside guests by default, but its Help Center says that on Team plans Claude can join those calls by default. Check the setting before a sales or client call, and tell people they are being transcribed.
  • Regulated data. Sheets does not yet support HIPAA, CMEK or zero data retention, Whiteboards is not available to HIPAA-ready organizations, and Meetings is not available to organizations with zero data retention, HIPAA-ready setups or CMEK.
  • Records. Deleting a Claude Doc is permanent, with no trash, and edits and comments inside a doc are not yet in the Compliance API (Docs guide).
  • Add-ins. In Google Workspace, Claude sees only the file you open it in plus the connectors you turn on, within your existing Google sharing permissions (Google add-on page). In Outlook, drafts and invites wait for you to click send (Microsoft add-in page).

For comparison, the Google pricing page says company data in Gemini chat is not used to train models, and Microsoft lists Enterprise Data Protection in Copilot Business.

Who should add it, and who should wait

With no email or file storage service, switching here means adding Claude next to your current suite. It fits:

  • Teams on Google Workspace that meet in Google Meet, because Meetings works there today and the Google add-on brings Claude into Docs and Sheets.
  • Teams that handle both Microsoft and Google files, since one seat covers both add-ins.
  • Solo owners, who get every app except Meetings and Motion on Pro.
  • Teams already paying for Claude, since the apps add no new line item.

Wait if your calls run on Zoom or Microsoft Teams: Anthropic says other video platforms are coming but gives no date. Wait if your finance work needs pivot tables, macros or more than 100,000 cells; keep that model in Excel and use the Excel add-in. Wait if you handle health data or need zero retention, given the beta exclusions above. And a Microsoft-only office happy with Copilot would be paying for a second assistant.

How to trial it without a long contract

  1. Start free. Docs, Slides and Design cost $0 on the Free plan (pricing).
  2. Let one person test the paid apps on Pro with monthly billing at $20. That covers Sheets, Whiteboards, Data and both add-ins.
  3. Install the add-ins your team needs: the Microsoft one from AppSource through the Microsoft admin center (deployment notes), or the Google one from the Google Workspace Marketplace (setup).
  4. To test Meetings, you need Team, which starts at 2 people, so two standard seats on monthly billing cost $50 for a month. The pricing table lists no trial for Team or self-serve Enterprise; only sales-assisted Enterprise shows trials.
  5. Test on real work: one weekly report in Docs, one tracker in Sheets and one internal meeting, then decide.

By contrast, Microsoft offers a one-month free trial that needs a credit card and turns into a paid plan, and Google offers 14 days at no cost.

What to do this week

  • Enterprise admins: Claude Data turns on by default on November 20, 2026 (launch post). Decide in Organization settings, Artifacts, before then.
  • Team owners: Data, Sheets and Whiteboards are on from day one and Meetings is in Organization settings, Products. Check external sharing and the Meetings guest setting.
  • Standalone Design users: move your design systems before the old site closes on December 14 (migration notes).
  • Everyone: pick one recurring task, such as a weekly report or a budget, and run it through the suite for two weeks before you buy seats for the whole team.

faqs: What is Anthropic's office suite called?

Anthropic does not call it an office suite. The apps inside Claude are called Artifacts: Claude Docs, Slides, Design, Data, Sheets, Whiteboards and Motion. Claude Meetings is a separate beta, and the add-ins are Claude for Microsoft 365 and Claude for Google Workspace.
No. Claude Sheets is in beta on the Pro, Max, Ultra, Team and Enterprise plans. Pro costs $17 a month billed yearly or $20 monthly. The Free plan includes Claude Docs, Slides and Design.
How much does Claude Meetings cost?

Claude Meetings needs a Team or Enterprise plan. A Team standard seat is $20 a month billed yearly or $25 monthly, for 2 to 150 people. During the beta, notes, transcripts and answers that do not use connected tools are included, and docs and whiteboards made in a call are free through February 10, 2027.
Can Claude work inside Excel and Google Sheets?

Yes. Claude for Microsoft 365 works in Excel, PowerPoint and Word on all paid plans, with Outlook in beta. Claude for Google Workspace is in beta on all paid plans and works in Google Docs, Sheets and Slides.
Anthropic's May 7, 2026 post says Microsoft 365 Copilot customers can use Claude models directly in Excel and PowerPoint. Claude for Microsoft 365 can also connect through Microsoft Foundry.
Does Anthropic train its models on my documents?

On Team and Enterprise plans, not by default, unless someone sends feedback with the thumbs buttons. On Free, Pro and Max, chats are used to improve models if you allow it in your privacy settings, and incognito chats are not used.
